background.text: The Florentine constitution barred the old nobility from office and opened power only to guild members: a merchant republic in form. Behind the machinery of sortition and short terms of office ran the factional contest of the great families, and from Cosimo onward the Medici governed as monarchs in substance while preserving the republican frame. A city without mineral resources sought its survival not in territorial conquest but in the multiplier of trade and exchange; the branch networks of the Bardi, Peruzzi, and Medici banks, stretching from London to the Black Sea, generated the surplus wealth on which workshop production and patronage rested. Training in Verrocchio's workshop was a comprehensive education of the bottega: casting, metallurgy, and surveying alongside painting. The 1472 enrollment marks his qualification as an independent master, yet the 1476 denunciation shows him still living under Verrocchio's roof. The commissions that documents can fix, the San Bernardo altarpiece of 1478, never begun, and the Adoration of 1481, abandoned at the underpainting, share a single trait: neither was completed. That fact is itself a source for Leonardo's position in the Florentine market of his first period.
